companies.name: Nedap
companies.summary: Electronic systems and software · Groenlo, Netherlands
companies.description: Develops and manufactures electronic systems and software for healthcare, identification (RFID), light controls and livestock management. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam. Headquartered in Groenlo, Gelderland, with 1,077 employees at the end of 2025.

companies.name: Alfen
companies.summary: Smart grids, energy storage and EV charging · Almere, Netherlands
signals: designs, develops and produces energy storage systems
companies.description: Designs, develops, produces and services smart grid solutions, energy storage systems and electric vehicle charging equipment. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam. Headquartered in Almere, with around 1,000 employees.

companies.name: Avantium
companies.summary: Renewable and circular chemistry · Amsterdam, Netherlands
signals: first commercial plant for FDCA in Delfzijl
companies.description: Chemical technology company developing renewable and circular polymers and chemistry. Its first commercial plant for FDCA, the building block of the plant-based plastic PEF, in Delfzijl was partly commissioned in 2025. Headquartered in Amsterdam, 259 FTE at the end of 2025. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam.

companies.name: Sunfire
companies.description: Develops and manufactures industrial electrolysers for green hydrogen (alkaline and solid oxide) and power-to-liquids. Headquarters and production in Dresden, with production in Solingen and Magdeburg. Over 700 employees. Is investing about EUR 30 million in an R&D centre at its Dresden site.

companies.name: Härterei Reese (group)
companies.summary: Heat treatment of steel components · four sites in Germany
companies.description: Family-owned heat-treatment group (hardening, nitriding and annealing of steel components) with four sites in Germany: Bochum, Brackenheim, Weimar and Chemnitz. Headcount is reported as roughly 240 to 280 depending on the source, with about EUR 40 million turnover. It runs over 200 heat-treatment installations and reports several projects and investments planned to save energy, including a building permit for a new surface-hardening shop.
